value.description: No genes worth logging. A baseliner works like your grandfather worked — hands, sweat, and whatever tool's in reach. Cheap to feed, easy to trust, nothing to trade for. Every clan's got a few; every clan needs them.

No genes worth logging. A baseliner works like your grandfather worked — hands, sweat, and whatever tool's in reach. Cheap to feed, easy to trust, nothing to trade for. Every clan's got a few; every clan needs them.

Gray-skinned, made for the dark—drop one in a mine shaft or a wrecked hull's crawlspace and they'll out-dig anyone topside. Bad eyes past arm's reach, and the desert sun will blind them faster than it blinds you. Keep them under the crawler, not on watch.

Gray-skinned, made for the dark—drop one in a mine shaft or a wrecked hull's crawlspace and they'll out-dig anyone topside. Bad eyes past arm's reach, and the desert sun will blind them faster than it blinds you. Keep them under the crawler, not on watch.

Thin-boned and calm as still water, a genie will read a busted engine faster than you can strip the panel off it. Don't send them to haggle—they'll say the wrong thing and not know why—and don't hit them; they break easy and it takes them a long time to stop feeling it.

Pretty, warm, good at reading a room and worse than useless in a fight—some clans keep them for the trade table, some just keep them. We don't put a wrench in their hands; we put them across from a buyer who's decided he doesn't like our price.

Red-eyed and built for the fight, not the crew. Heals fast, doesn't flinch, and needs go-juice in its blood or it starts to come apart—keep the supply steady or don't bother owning one. Doesn't make small talk. Doesn't need to.

Red-eyed and built for the fight, not the crew. Heals fast, doesn't flinch, and needs go-juice in its blood or it starts to come apart—keep the supply steady or don't bother owning one. Doesn't make small talk. Doesn't need to.

Horned and quick as a scared varmint, an impid crosses open sand faster than anything else that walks—and can spit fire while doing it. Useless behind a plow, weak once someone gets in close. Send them ahead, not to hold the line.

Built like the underside of a sandcrawler—hard to hurt, hard to talk sense into. Give them the heavy work and don't expect the ledger-keeping. Quick to anger, slow to forget it.
Built like the underside of a sandcrawler—hard to hurt, hard to talk sense into. Give them the heavy work and don't expect the ledger-keeping. Quick to anger, slow to forget it.

Trotter-handed and iron-stomached, a pigskin will eat what would kill the rest of the crew and never miss a meal. Don't hand them fine tools—those hands weren't made for it—but hand them the detonator and stand back; they've got a taste for it.

Doesn't age, barely dies, heals like the desert doesn't touch it—and needs the blood of the free peoples to keep living, which is the kind of debt no clan wants on its ledger. Rare enough we've only heard the stories. Burn first, ask later.

Grey-skinned and mean, a waster can walk through poison air that would drop the rest of us in a minute—so long as it's got its psychite. No sickness touches it either. Doesn't make it pleasant company.

Grey-skinned and mean, a waster can walk through poison air that would drop the rest of us in a minute—so long as it's got its psychite. No sickness touches it either. Doesn't make it pleasant company.

Big, furred, and built for a cold none of us have ever felt—wrong coat for this desert, but nobody outworks one once it gets moving. Talks to animals like they're crew. Outsiders call them dumb for it; we've seen what that trick's worth in a fight.

Big, furred, and built for a cold none of us have ever felt—wrong coat for this desert, but nobody outworks one once it gets moving. Talks to animals like they're crew. Outsiders call them dumb for it; we've seen what that trick's worth in a fight.

Big, tusked, from a wet green world that ruined them for a desert. Strong backs, short patience — put them on hauling and lifting, never on a delicate deal. Feed them well and they won't ask questions about where the meat came from.

Big, tusked, from a wet green world that ruined them for a desert. Strong backs, short patience — put them on hauling and lifting, never on a delicate deal. Feed them well and they won't ask questions about where the meat came from.

Long dangling tendrils off the face, catch the wind before you feel it — useful on watch duty during a storm. Steady, easygoing types, good with their hands, don't spook at a hard bargain. Homeworld gets battered by weather worse than ours, so a little grit doesn't slow them down.

Old. Older than they look, and that's the problem — they feed on more than food, and every settlement that's ever hosted one long-term has a story it doesn't like to tell. Charming to a fault, which is exactly the warning sign. Trade in the open, never alone, never after dark.

Round black eyes, thick fur, a temper that doesn't wait for an insult to land before it swings. Some strains run four arms — twice the work, twice the reach in a brawl. Good muscle for a raid or a hauling crew; bad choice to seat across a negotiating table.

Round black eyes, thick fur, a temper that doesn't wait for an insult to land before it swings. Some strains run four arms — twice the work, twice the reach in a brawl. Good muscle for a raid or a hauling crew; bad choice to seat across a negotiating table.

Pale skin, white hair, eyes that don't blink at a gene-splice most folk would call heresy. Their homeworld bred engineers who rewrote living things for a living, and it shows in how coldly they talk about a body. Worth more at a workbench than a campfire.

Pale skin, white hair, eyes that don't blink at a gene-splice most folk would call heresy. Their homeworld bred engineers who rewrote living things for a living, and it shows in how coldly they talk about a body. Worth more at a workbench than a campfire.

Domed skull, no eyelids, ears that catch a coolant hiss three rooms off before you do. Steady hands, careful minds, half of them can carry a tune while they work a torch. Put one on watch or on repairs and forget you're short-handed.

Domed skull, no eyelids, ears that catch a coolant hiss three rooms off before you do. Steady hands, careful minds, half of them can carry a tune while they work a torch. Put one on watch or on repairs and forget you're short-handed.

Fur that shifts color with the mood, and a mind that never stops keeping score. Every clan trades gossip, but a Bothan trades it for a living — what they know, they sell, and what they sell, someone usually dies over. Useful. Never fully trusted, and they'd tell you the same.

Fur that shifts color with the mood, and a mind that never stops keeping score. Every clan trades gossip, but a Bothan trades it for a living — what they know, they sell, and what they sell, someone usually dies over. Useful. Never fully trusted, and they'd tell you the same.

Feline, quick-tempered, and loyal past the point of sense once you've earned it. A slight lands harder on a Cathar than on most — keep the insults for someone else's crew. Good in a fight, better as kin.

Feline, quick-tempered, and loyal past the point of sense once you've earned it. A slight lands harder on a Cathar than on most — keep the insults for someone else's crew. Good in a fight, better as kin.

Tall skull, two minds working under it, and they'll make you wait while both weigh in. Slow to decide, near impossible to fool once they have. Put them on planning a raid or reading a contract, not on the clock.

Tall skull, two minds working under it, and they'll make you wait while both weigh in. Slow to decide, near impossible to fool once they have. Put them on planning a raid or reading a contract, not on the clock.

Barely knee-high on a human, ears like satellite dishes, nose that reads a chemfuel leak before the gauge does. Quick, nervous, good in tight crawlspaces a bigger scavenger can't reach. Kin to how we work, if not to what we are.

Barely knee-high on a human, ears like satellite dishes, nose that reads a chemfuel leak before the gauge does. Quick, nervous, good in tight crawlspaces a bigger scavenger can't reach. Kin to how we work, if not to what we are.

Blue skin, head-tresses that read a room's mood before the mouth does, and a homeworld that was all water. They wilt on long dry runs faster than they'll admit — keep the ration skins close. Dignified, careful traders once they trust you.

Blue skin, head-tresses that read a room's mood before the mouth does, and a homeworld that was all water. They wilt on long dry runs faster than they'll admit — keep the ration skins close. Dignified, careful traders once they trust you.

Blue skin, red eyes, and a stare that's already three moves ahead of the conversation. Come from somewhere cold and unmapped, and it left them formal, disciplined, slow to warm to strangers. Deal straight with a Chiss and they'll deal straighter back — cross one and they'll have planned for it before you tried.

Blue skin, red eyes, and a stare that's already three moves ahead of the conversation. Come from somewhere cold and unmapped, and it left them formal, disciplined, slow to warm to strangers. Deal straight with a Chiss and they'll deal straighter back — cross one and they'll have planned for it before you tried.

Horns on the males, wild manes on the females, and a homeworld thick with old magic nobody here claims to understand. Hard folk, harder to spook — most have already survived worse than a desert. Respect the reputation even when the individual seems ordinary.

Horns on the males, wild manes on the females, and a homeworld thick with old magic nobody here claims to understand. Hard folk, harder to spook — most have already survived worse than a desert. Respect the reputation even when the individual seems ordinary.

Fur that eats the light instead of reflecting it — step into shadow and they're near gone. Nocturnal by nature, which suits a night salvage run better than any tool we own. Post one on a dark watch and sleep easier.

Fur that eats the light instead of reflecting it — step into shadow and they're near gone. Nocturnal by nature, which suits a night salvage run better than any tool we own. Post one on a dark watch and sleep easier.

Horns and a devil's grin on the males, a face fur-covered enough to fool a stranger on the females — neither means what an outsider assumes. Restless by blood; most left home and never went back, which makes them the crew that never balks at a long run. Wanderers, not villains, whatever the face suggests.

Horns and a devil's grin on the males, a face fur-covered enough to fool a stranger on the females — neither means what an outsider assumes. Restless by blood; most left home and never went back, which makes them the crew that never balks at a long run. Wanderers, not villains, whatever the face suggests.

Smooth blue skin, no nose worth mentioning, red eyes that never seem to blink at a bad flight path. Some of the first to fly among the stars, and it's bred true — put a Duros in the pilot's seat of anything that moves and trust the landing.

Smooth blue skin, no nose worth mentioning, red eyes that never seem to blink at a bad flight path. Some of the first to fly among the stars, and it's bred true — put a Duros in the pilot's seat of anything that moves and trust the landing.

Pale skin, white hair, silver eyes, and a way of reading a fight in the set of your shoulders before you throw a punch. Warrior stock, disciplined past what most clans bother with. Hire one to guard the haul and don't waste words explaining the job — they'll already be watching the door.

Small, furry, and don't let the size fool you — a cornered Ewok has killed things twice its weight with a sharpened stick and a good trap. Tribal, clannish, suspicious of strangers the same way we are. Closer kin to us than most bigger folk want to admit.

Small, furry, and don't let the size fool you — a cornered Ewok has killed things twice its weight with a sharpened stick and a good trap. Tribal, clannish, suspicious of strangers the same way we are. Closer kin to us than most bigger folk want to admit.

Mottled green skin, ridged skull, and a way of smelling out exactly what you want to hear — some claim it's more than charm, that the scent itself works on you. Watch a deal with a Falleen the same way you'd watch a card game with a cheat: closely, and sober.

Tendrils trailing off the head and face, and enough years ahead of them — some run four centuries — that a Feeorin remembers debts the rest of us forgot were owed. Patient past reason. Good for a long trade relationship, bad to try and cheat, because they will still be here to collect.

Tendrils trailing off the head and face, and enough years ahead of them — some run four centuries — that a Feeorin remembers debts the rest of us forgot were owed. Patient past reason. Good for a long trade relationship, bad to try and cheat, because they will still be here to collect.

Tusked, thick-skinned, built for lifting what two of us couldn't. Not the crew for talking a price down, but put one on the door or the loading ramp and nothing gets past that shouldn't. Feed them plenty and they're no trouble at all.

Tusked, thick-skinned, built for lifting what two of us couldn't. Not the crew for talking a price down, but put one on the door or the loading ramp and nothing gets past that shouldn't. Feed them plenty and they're no trouble at all.

Some breathe our air fine; some need a mask the moment they step off a ship, ammonia-bred and none too happy about the swap. The findsmen among them won't say the word 'I' — track a person's trail their whole life and start talking like the trail matters more than the tracker. Hire one to find something lost and don't ask how they do it.

Hire one to find something lost and don't ask how they do it.

Winged, insectoid, and never really individuals — deal with the hive's will, not the drone in front of you, or the deal means nothing past that one drone. Master builders; put a swarm of them on a foundry job and they'll outbuild a whole crew of us. Don't turn your back on the wings.

Amphibious, thick-skinned, and clumsier looking than they fight — a Gungan with an energy-ball launcher has ended arguments faster than a blaster. Need water near enough to duck into, and they'll grumble the whole desert crossing about the lack of it. Sturdier allies than the look suggests.

Hulking, black-skinned, built like they were meant for open water or open space rather than dry ground — which, on this world, they mostly were. Rare out here, and worth it when you find one: nothing hauls heavier or takes a hit better. Thick hide, thicker patience.

Slow-moving, slug-bodied, and it doesn't matter — a Hutt never has to move to win a deal, because the deal was already decided before you sat down. Old, patient past a human lifetime twice over, and every credit that crosses their coils gets remembered. Never owe one anything you can't repay on their terms.

Old, patient past a human lifetime twice over, and every credit that crosses their coils gets remembered. Never owe one anything you can't repay on their terms.

Curved horns, reddish skin, and some of them swear they see trouble coming before it arrives — a few are even right often enough to bet on it. Good scouts, better gamblers. Listen when one says to move the caravan; ask questions after.

Curved horns, reddish skin, and some of them swear they see trouble coming before it arrives — a few are even right often enough to bet on it. Good scouts, better gamblers. Listen when one says to move the caravan; ask questions after.

Crown of horns aside, near enough to human that you'd miss it in a headwrap. Homeworld's as unforgiving as ours, so they take to this life without complaint — desert-bred stock knows desert-bred work.

Crown of horns aside, near enough to human that you'd miss it in a headwrap. Homeworld's as unforgiving as ours, so they take to this life without complaint — desert-bred stock knows desert-bred work.

Long-necked, two mouths, a voice that comes out low and doubled like it's speaking from two directions at once. Gentle by nature, and they'll wince at how hard we strip a scrapyard bare — keep them off any job that looks too much like ruining living ground. Peaceable, useful, easily offended by waste.

Long-necked, two mouths, a voice that comes out low and doubled like it's speaking from two directions at once. Gentle by nature, and they'll wince at how hard we strip a scrapyard bare — keep them off any job that looks too much like ruining living ground. Peaceable, useful, easily offended by waste.

Small, fur-covered, orange eyes that glow under a hood — a desert people, same as us, who never stop moving from one dry world to the next that'll have them. Every clan out here is built the same way: salvage what the big folk left, trade what you can't use, keep the hood up and the eyes hidden. Family, more or less, whatever crawler they call home.

Reptilian, scarred, and most wear the skull of something they killed rather than talk about how. Their homeworld chewed them into warriors first and everything else second. Earn respect from a Kaleesh with steel, not silver — credits mean less to them than a kill well made.

Tall, thin, amphibian, and colder about a living body than anyone ought to be — they didn't just study cloning, they perfected it. Precise, clinical, unnervingly patient with a scalpel. Good to have around when someone's hurt bad; don't expect warmth while they work.

Orange-skinned, big black goggle-eyes too sensitive for open sun, and they need a mask fitted the moment they leave homeworld air or they won't last the day. Once geared up, sharp senses and steady nerves — good trackers, better pilots. Budget the mask into the price of hiring one.

Green to brown skin, green blood if they're cut, and a build made for a lifetime of hauling somebody else's cargo. Strong, uncomplaining workers — the Hutts have leaned on their backs for generations, and we're not too proud to do the same. Don't flinch at the blood; it's just theirs.

Long snout, keen nose — a Kubaz can smell a coolant leak or a lie three stalls down the bazaar. Keep an eye on the ledger around one; the good ones traded gossip and grudges as fast as scrap back on Kubindi, and habits like that don't stay home. Useful on a crew that needs eyes and ears in a crowded market.

Useful on a crew that needs eyes and ears in a crowded market.

Big, strong, and built for hauling what two of us together couldn't lift. Lasan is gone — burned out from under them by the Empire — so don't ask, and don't expect gratitude for pity; earn trust with fair work and a straight trade, same as anyone who's lost a homeworld.

Mud-world stock, and it shows: they'll work a swamp claim or a flooded trench without the complaint that would fold a desert crew in an hour. Mimban bred them fighting Imperial mining rigs, so don't be surprised if one still flinches at a company logo.

Green or purple skin, marks cut into the face for things earned, not given — respect that, it's the closest thing they've got to our own clan-marks. Quiet, disciplined, good with their hands; the kind you want on a delicate salvage job, not a loud one.

Big-domed heads, gill-slits, a nose for a bad hull weld from a klick off. Put one near a busted engine or a leaking tank before you put a wrench in your own hand — Mon Cala breeds shipwrights, and it shows in everything they touch.

Big-domed heads, gill-slits, a nose for a bad hull weld from a klick off. Put one near a busted engine or a leaking tank before you put a wrench in your own hand — Mon Cala breeds shipwrights, and it shows in everything they touch.

Thin, tall, and they'll count your credits twice before you've finished counting them once. Banking-clan blood; fair dealers if the terms are exact, but read every line before you sign — a Muun never writes a contract that favors the other side.

Thin, tall, and they'll count your credits twice before you've finished counting them once. Banking-clan blood; fair dealers if the terms are exact, but read every line before you sign — a Muun never writes a contract that favors the other side.

Tall, quick, and touchy about honor in a way that gets men killed over nothing, so don't insult one you mean to keep around. Wild Space stock, hard fighters, harder to read — useful backup, bad company for a slow argument.

Tall, quick, and touchy about honor in a way that gets men killed over nothing, so don't insult one you mean to keep around. Wild Space stock, hard fighters, harder to read — useful backup, bad company for a slow argument.

Green-blue skin, head-tentacles that read the air like a Jawa reads a scrap pile — don't try to bluff one, they'll smell the lie before you finish it. Amphibious, tough in weather that'd cook the rest of us; good for the wet-season runs nobody else wants.

Smooth green faces, soft voices, and a mind for profit margins sharper than any blade on this crew. Trade Federation stock — don't mistake the caution for weakness, it's kept their kind rich longer than most species stay solvent.

Smooth green faces, soft voices, and a mind for profit margins sharper than any blade on this crew. Trade Federation stock — don't mistake the caution for weakness, it's kept their kind rich longer than most species stay solvent.
Blue fur, wolf jaw, claws that'll open a crate faster than a vibroblade. Not much for words, plenty for work — point one at a job and step back.
Blue fur, wolf jaw, claws that'll open a crate faster than a vibroblade. Not much for words, plenty for work — point one at a job and step back.

Scaled hide, horns, built for rough work in worse weather — Kintan bred them tough. Plenty hire out as muscle for the Hutts; that's not an insult, it's just where the steady credits are, and a Nikto on your side is worth the wage.

Scaled hide, horns, built for rough work in worse weather — Kintan bred them tough. Plenty hire out as muscle for the Hutts; that's not an insult, it's just where the steady credits are, and a Nikto on your side is worth the wage.

Soft, round, big ears, gentler than they look — good ears for a haggle, bad stomach for a fight. Feed one well and it'll remember you kindly; Ortolans hold a grudge about hunger longer than they hold one about anything else.

Soft, round, big ears, gentler than they look — good ears for a haggle, bad stomach for a fight. Feed one well and it'll remember you kindly; Ortolans hold a grudge about hunger longer than they hold one about anything else.

Blue skin, gold marks on the face, cold-world stock that handles heat worse than we do — keep one shaded and watered on a desert run or you'll lose the day's work to sunstroke. Steady traders otherwise, no complaints there.

Blue skin, gold marks on the face, cold-world stock that handles heat worse than we do — keep one shaded and watered on a desert run or you'll lose the day's work to sunstroke. Steady traders otherwise, no complaints there.

Big skull, small face, and a look that unsettles half the market before they've said a word. Spice-cartel blood runs deep in that family name — trade careful, ask fewer questions than you want to, and never owe one credits.

Big skull, small face, and a look that unsettles half the market before they've said a word. Spice-cartel blood runs deep in that family name — trade careful, ask fewer questions than you want to, and never owe one credits.

Squid-faced, sharp-tempered about their old rivalry with the Mon Calamari — don't seat the two at the same table unless you like shouting. Good hands underwater or in a flooded hold; keep the grudge off the work floor and they're solid.

Squid-faced, sharp-tempered about their old rivalry with the Mon Calamari — don't seat the two at the same table unless you like shouting. Good hands underwater or in a flooded hold; keep the grudge off the work floor and they're solid.

Amphibious, old-blood, and carry themselves like they remember when their people ruled the stars — some of the oldest hyperspace lore in the galaxy traces back to Lehon. Rare to see one on a scavenger crew; when you do, listen before you talk.

Amphibious, old-blood, and carry themselves like they remember when their people ruled the stars — some of the oldest hyperspace lore in the galaxy traces back to Lehon. Rare to see one on a scavenger crew; when you do, listen before you talk.

Big infrared eyes, twitchy antennae that pick up a footstep before your own ears do — good watch on a night haul. Rodia turns out hunters and trackers more than traders; pay the bounty, don't become one.

Big infrared eyes, twitchy antennae that pick up a footstep before your own ears do — good watch on a night haul. Rodia turns out hunters and trackers more than traders; pay the bounty, don't become one.

Water-skinned, from a whole world of the stuff, and they wilt fast away from it — keep a basin or a damp cloth handy if one's working your crew in this desert, or you'll lose them to the dry faster than you'd think. Steady, careful workers once they're not dying of thirst.

Water-skinned, from a whole world of the stuff, and they wilt fast away from it — keep a basin or a damp cloth handy if one's working your crew in this desert, or you'll lose them to the dry faster than you'd think. Steady, careful workers once they're not dying of thirst.

Red skin, priest-caste bearing, and a way of talking about the dark side like it's a tool on a belt rather than a story. Rare out this far — if one's trading with you, they want something specific, and it's worth finding out what before the deal closes.

Red skin, priest-caste bearing, and a way of talking about the dark side like it's a tool on a belt rather than a story. Rare out this far — if one's trading with you, they want something specific, and it's worth finding out what before the deal closes.

Ridged red hide, tendrils down the jaw, built for a fight rather than a sermon — different line from the priest-caste Kissai, same old blood. Hard workers when the job's physical; don't expect the patience for anything fine.

The engineer line of that old bloodline — tomb-builders and shipwrights once, and the hands still show for it. Give one a busted hull or a collapsed tunnel and they'll have opinions worth listening to.

Big nostrils, a jaw with a pair of tusks, and a face that reads sadder than the pawn usually feels — don't mistake the look for the mood. Decent traders, expressive in a way that makes them easy to read at the table, which cuts both ways.

Big eyes, big ears, built for the dark of a mine tunnel or a ship's crawlspace — Sullust breeds them underground and it never leaves. Some of the best small-craft pilots you'll find; put one behind the stick before you put one on a wrench.

Old blood, near enough to a ghost story as a living species gets — the tales say they're kin somewhere far back to the armored clans, but nobody out here can prove it and I wouldn't ask one to their face. If you meet one, you're meeting something rare.

Big cats standing upright, digitigrade like they're always ready to run — strong, fast, dangerous to cross. Good hunters, better guards; don't leave food unclaimed around one and don't test the claws.

Colored skin, white stripes, head-tails that hear better than most crews' whole watch rotation put together. Shili bred them for the hunt-pack — one of these on lookout is worth two without the montrals.

Scaled, tough, and they'll grow a lost finger back before you've finished apologizing for costing it to them. Hunters by nature and old rivals of the Wookiees — keep the two off the same crew unless you enjoy refereeing.

Wrapped head to foot, never seen bare-faced by outsiders and don't expect to be the first. Tatooine's own — territorial, dangerous to a moisture farm or a careless caravan, about as likely to trade fair as a sandstorm is to hold still. Respect the wraps, keep your distance, don't push.

Lekku instead of hair, from Ryloth, and more of them scattered across the galaxy in chains than free — a fact worth remembering before you make demands of one on this crew. Adaptable, quick-witted, and they've earned every bit of the wariness they carry.

Short, piggish snout, and they'll outwork three of us on a shift without slowing down — Cloud City bred them for exactly that kind of labor and the habit never left. Pay fair, work them fair, and you'll never find a steadier hand on the line.

Pale skin, no color in the eyes, and a soft way of talking that can turn a bad deal into a good-sounding one before you notice — watch for that, not the face. Umbara's a dark world; don't be surprised if one prefers the shade.

Leather hide, tough enough to shrug off sun and a stray blaster bolt both — desert stock knows desert stock, and a Weequay handles this heat better than half the crew. Plenty run with pirates or mercs back where they're from; that's a resume, not a warning, out here.

Tall, strong, covered in fur, and loyal to whoever's earned it — Kashyyyk breeds warriors and craftsmen both, and you want either on your side of a fight. Don't cheat one on a debt; a Wookiee's memory for a wrong is as long as the arm that'll collect it.

Rare enough that most of the clan's never traded with one — small, strange, said to live long past anything reasonable. Whatever the truth of it, treat the meeting as the find of a lifetime and don't try too hard to explain what you're looking at.

Red skin, near-human otherwise, and they'll feel the room's mood before you've finished walking into it — good for reading a tense trade, bad for keeping your own bluff hidden. Warm company, sharp senses; don't bring one to a negotiation you plan to lie through.

Feline, sharp-featured, carrying an old reputation for the slave trade that the honest ones spend a lifetime living down. Judge the pawn in front of you, not the empire behind the name — but don't be shocked if others on the crew aren't as willing to let it go.

Pale and thin, built for the black between worlds, not the ground under it—vacuum barely slows one down, but ask it to haul or swing a blade and it comes up short. Good for gravship hull work; nobody else wants the job that bad.

Scaled and cold-blooded, spliced for dry country same as we chose it—handles the heat better than most and doesn't miss the company. Harsh voice, short patience for outsiders. We understand each other on that much.
